design_rationale:
WORKLOG — task 1 of season_pass_billing_desk (Granite Ridge Mountain Collective, passes).

STEP 0. Draw, taken before the design:
  .venv/bin/python skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0004_ski_resort_operator/tasks/season_pass_billing_desk --task 1
  {"task": 1, "key": "ski_resort_operator/season_pass_billing_desk/1", "prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [6, 4, 6]}
  Two prerequisite problems besides the root; the three computations carry 6, 4 and 6 factors. Assignment:
  passes_ext_credit_offset 4, passes_ext_cancellation_charge 6, passes_ext_settlement_credit 6.

ASSET LEDGER. Task 0 occupied the arrears recovery, the restoration charge and the carry-forward fee, with
  collect_past_due_0159c539, restore_pass_scanning_08275b43 and elect_pass_carry_forward_09e30d1a, and the base
  lineage passes_installment_plan, passes_arrears_suspension and passes_deferral. This task claims the credit side
  and the surrender: passes_ext_credit_offset, passes_ext_cancellation_charge and passes_ext_settlement_credit with
  apply_pass_credit_52fe36c9, give_up_season_pass_8c1a0eca and issue_settlement_credit_d3237287, on the lineage
  passes_credit_redemption and passes_cancellation_refund. The two scopes share no policy, no tool and no base
  policy, and together they cover every extended policy in the charter, which closes the difficulty.

WHY IT MAKES A GOOD TEST. The caller asks one thing: whatever the collective will put back to him on a pass he can no longer pay for. The terms tell a
  solver that the credit issued on a surrender waits on the charge retained standing on the pass account, and that
  the charge retained waits on the resort credit standing on the record having been applied against what the account
  still has to collect. Neither the credit standing nor the application is anything the caller knows. On top of that
  the pass record's own running credit figure understates the ledger by the 45.00 billing-error entry, so an agent
  who reads the record rather than reconciling the entries gets the first figure wrong and every figure after it;
  and the six lift scan entries fall on five dates, so an agent who counts dates rather than the entries the rules name drops a tier twice.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD.
  Write 1 (subject passes_credit_redeem, governed by passes_credit_redemption):
    credit_within_validity (time). Anchor 'the credit was issued'; source passes_ledger.event_date; relation
    not_after; duration variants.credit_validity_days = 365 for the Collective Unlimited tier; day zero is the issue
    day; boundary inclusive. The entry drawn against was issued 2026-12-28, so the last day is 2027-12-28 and the
    handling date is the ninth day. Negative case: an application on 2027-12-29 is out.
    credit_record_state (state): the record must not have reached the cancelled or closed state, and it stands
    active — which is also why the application must come before the surrender and not after it.
  Write 2 (subject passes_cancel, governed by passes_cancellation_refund):
    inside_cancellation_window (time). Anchor 'the pass application was recorded'; source
    passes_holdings.applied_date; relation not_after; duration variants.cancellation_window_days = 30; boundary
    inclusive. Applied 2026-12-09, last day 2027-01-08, handling date the twenty-eighth day. Negative case: a
    surrender on 2027-01-09 brings nothing back at all.
    medical_claim_settled (authorization): the protection records show a settled claim on a plan held by this
    household, so the gate is satisfied on its own terms; the surrender itself is given on the loss of employment,
    for which the condition does not bite, and the plan record is nevertheless what the surrender is recorded
    against.
    not_already_given_up (dedup): the record stands active with no cancellation reason, so it has not been given up
    before.
  Write 3 (subject passes_credit_issue, governed by passes_cancellation_refund): medical_claim_settled alone, on
    the same protection record.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. One pass record: the Collective Unlimited pass registered to Alan Whitcombe for 2026-27,
  correlation key passes_holdings.pass_id, and one protection plan written over that very pass, correlation key
  insure_holdings.protection_plan_id. The credit application is correlated to the single credit entry it is drawn
  against through passes_ledger.pass_event_id. The two credit entries are distinguished by the reason each was
  issued for: the service-recovery entry of 2026-12-28 is drawn on, the billing-error entry of 2027-01-02 is held
  back, and the record's own credit figure of 260.00 counts neither of them correctly.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD.
  Root: passes_ext_settlement_credit. Prerequisites: passes_ext_cancellation_charge, and behind it
  passes_ext_credit_offset. A chain of three problems, two prerequisite problems, matching the draw.
  Edge A (settlement credit waits on the surrender charge), kind value_input, gate retained_offset_rate, form state.
    Sentence: 'The resort credit issued when a pass is given up is worked out only after the pass account carries the
    charge retained on the pass being given up.' Four-point test: (1) 'only after' joins this policy's own result to
    what it waits on; (2) the thing waited on is a record-visible state, a charge entry standing on the pass account;
    (3) no tool, policy id or code token; (4) the strength matches the edge. Exactly one write of this difficulty
    books that charge: the cancellation charge policy's own rule is the only one that places a charge retained on a
    pass being given up. Derivation: the sentence names the state; the ledger shows no such charge; the cancellation
    charge rule is what books it; so that write is the resolving action.
  Edge B (surrender charge waits on the credit application), kind value_input, gate outstanding_rate, form state.
    Sentence: 'The charge retained when a pass is given up is worked out only after the pass account carries an
    application of resort credit against the amount it still shows to collect.' The same four points hold, and
    exactly one write of this difficulty books an application of resort credit against a pass account.
  Both edges are value_input. Deletion sensitivity from the Step 5 run: skipping the credit application moves the
  charge retained 321.70 -> 352.75; skipping the surrender moves the settlement credit 302.89 -> 640.68.

FACTOR CARD (figures from the Step 5 run).
  passes_ext_credit_offset, four factors, baseline 260.00 against gold 127.57:
    credit_pot_basis (method) 305.00 from the entries vs 260.00 from the record (93.82); schedule_stage_share
    (parameter) three quarters vs the whole (203.82); error_credit_hold (parameter) 45.00 held vs none (172.57);
    protection_premium_hold (parameter, cross-difficulty on insure) 56.18 held vs none (183.75). The cross-difficulty
    tier reads the premium still to be collected and the state of the plan written over this pass, both seeded on
    insure_holdings, with the protection account's own entries seeded behind them.
  passes_ext_cancellation_charge, six factors, baseline 150.00 against gold 321.70:
    charge_base_basis (method) 138.00 vs 150.00 (341.50); window_position_share (parameter) once and a half vs as it
    stands (245.80); outstanding_balance_share (parameter) once and a tenth vs as it stands (301.00);
    scan_component (parameter) 169.00 vs nothing (152.70); season_remaining_allowance (parameter) 25.00 vs
    nothing (346.70); protection_excess_relief (parameter, cross-difficulty) 50.00 vs nothing (371.70).
  passes_ext_settlement_credit, six factors, baseline 1014.39 against gold 302.89:
    remaining_share_basis (method) measured over the part of the season the holder had vs over the whole season
    (129.52); gross_back_basis (method) the pro rata basis on a scanned pass vs the standard method, that share
    less the tier's day use deduction taken once (143.19); scan_share (parameter) nine tenths vs as it stands (446.42); retained_charge_offset (parameter) the whole charge vs none (640.68); protection_payout_offset
    (parameter, cross-difficulty) the whole 620.00 vs nothing (953.89); credit_uplift (parameter) a twentieth vs none
    (288.47).
  Multi-source factors: error_credit_hold, whose every tier beyond the fall-through combines the error credit
  standing with the state of the pass record, and gross_back_basis, whose first tier combines the tier's refund basis with whether
  media was issued. Cross-difficulty factors: protection_premium_hold, protection_excess_relief and
  protection_payout_offset, reading the plan's state, its cover, its excess and its payouts.
  Near-misses: the stale credit figure on the record (260.00 against 305.00 in the entries); the two scans on
  2026-12-27, which make six entries on five dates and are counted as entries by the rules that read them; the cancellation window with two days left of thirty; and the
  season allowance boundary, where 102 days remaining against 149 clears two thirds by eight days.

SEED. Every row is load-bearing: the plan entry fixes what the outstanding amount is measured against and shows the
  schedule has not begun; the six lift scan entries are what the scan component and the scan share are counted from; the two credit entries are the pot, the error credit held
  back and the entry the application is drawn against; the protection plan carries three separate tiers and the
  protection account carries the payout that is taken off. The stale figure on passes_holdings.pass_credit_usd is the
  one deliberate discrepancy, declared here: the record shows 260.00 while the entries total 305.00, because the
  running figure was never moved when the billing-error credit was booked. The caller's own line, that he would
  rather the desk read it off their records than have him guess, is the natural re-check reaction that goes with it.
  Automatic clauses checked: the first instalment falls on the tier's tenth of the month no earlier than thirty days
  after the plan was opened, that is 2027-02-10, so no instalment has fallen due and none can be refused; the tier
  carries no blackout dates, so every scan stands; and the credit entries are inside the tier's 365-day validity.

PERSONA. Alan Whitcombe, a surveyor out of work since the second of January, businesslike and tired. He volunteers
  what the collective will put back to him, the job loss and that he skied a handful of days he cannot count, agreeing to the surrender only once the desk explains that nothing comes back until the pass is given up; he gives the mobile number, the
  date of birth and the passholder number when asked; he confirms the protection plan and the claim paid out but
  knows neither the plan's name nor the amount. His passive branches are: agreeing when told something must be put
  right first, accepting a charge without quarrelling, running the surrender himself when it is handed over, and
  closing once he is told the credit is on the record. He never states a figure, never orders the work and never
  corrects the agent.

STANDARD SOLUTION. Find the household by the mobile number; verify with two details; read the pass record, the whole
  pass account, the protection plan and the protection account; apply 127.57 of credit against what the account still
  has to collect, drawn against the service-recovery entry; hand the surrender to the customer, who gives the pass up
  on the loss of employment with 321.70 kept; then issue 302.89 of resort credit for what comes back.

VERIFICATION RUN (Step 5, executed): the harness replayed the gold writes with the real tools and evaluated each
  policy on the world standing before its own write.
  passes_ext_credit_offset result=127.57 (credit_on_record 260.0, recovery_credit 260.0, credit_issued_total 305.0,
    credit_drawn_total 0.0, error_credit 45.0, pot_usd 305.0, presented_count 0, refused_count 0, draw_share 0.75,
    retained_usd 45.0, premium_balance 56.18, protection_state claim_settled, premium_hold_usd 56.18, drawn_usd
    228.75); factor baselines 93.82 / 203.82 / 172.57 / 183.75; all-baseline 260.0.
  passes_ext_cancellation_charge result=321.70 (days_since_application 28, window_rate 1.5, plan_placed 1458.68,
    outstanding_share 0.9125, outstanding_rate 1.1, scans_taken 6, scan_component_usd 169.0, days_since_activation 27,
    charge_base_usd 138.0, season_days 149, season_left 102, season_allowance_usd 25.0, protection_cover_pct 80.0,
    protection_excess 50.0, protection_relief_usd 50.0); factor baselines 245.8 / 301.0 / 152.7 / 341.5 / 346.7 /
    371.7; all-baseline 150.0.
  passes_ext_settlement_credit result=302.90 (scans_counted 6, scan_entries 6, season_span 149, season_left_a 102, held_span 129,
    remaining_share 0.7907, gross_back_usd 1366.86, use_rate 0.9, retained_standing 321.7, retained_offset_rate 1.0,
    protection_payout 620.0, payout_offset_rate 1.0, plan_entries 1, uplift_rate 1.05, net_back_usd 288.47); factor
    baselines 129.52 / 143.20 / 446.42 / 640.69 / 953.90 / 288.48; all-baseline 1014.39.
  Prerequisite sensitivity in the same run: the charge retained without the credit application 352.75; the settlement
  credit without the surrender 640.68.

TWO-WAY SWEEP rule <-> compute. Forward: every binding that reads the world or chooses quotes its rule sentence, and
  the sensitive words line up — 'less every application already drawn' against the redeem sum, 'the pass record shows
  standing' against the record field, 'never more than the amount the pass account still shows to collect' against
  MN, 'never below zero' against MX, 'rounded to the cent once at the end' against the single closing RND, and 'the
  two amounts held back being deducted from that rounded figure rather than from the pot' against the order of the
  bindings. Backward: each rule sentence carrying a quantity, window, branch, ordering or rounding semantic is
  claimed by a binding — in the surrender charge, the two shares acting one after another and the components added
  and settled afterwards are pinned by the closing sentence and implemented in that order; in the settlement credit,
  the gross basis, the scan share, the two offsets and the uplift are each claimed, and the closing sentence
  fixes that the uplift acts on what the offsets leave rather than on the gross.

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT. With the extended yaml, the computes, the expected values and this
  worklog masked: the request is a surrender; the settlement rule says the credit waits on the charge retained
  standing; the surrender rule says the charge waits on an application of credit against what the account has to
  collect; the ledger shows two credit entries and no application; so the order is application, surrender,
  settlement. Reading the entries rather than the record's own figure gives the pot 305.00 and the three figures came
  out 127.57, 321.70 and 302.89, the same as gold. The two readings that could have differed — the record's credit
  figure and what is counted from the scan entries — are both settled against the ledger by the wording of
  the rules ('the sum of every credit entry the pass account shows issued', 'each day the pass account shows the
  holder took'), so no second reading survives.

CLOSURE. passes_ext_credit_offset -> apply_pass_credit_52fe36c9 -> computations[0] step 7 -> a passes_credit_redeem
  entry of 127.57, credit left 132.43, balance 1331.11; passes_ext_cancellation_charge ->
  give_up_season_pass_8c1a0eca -> computations[1] step 9 -> a cancellation charge of 321.70, status cancelled, closed
  date 2027-01-06, balance 1652.81; passes_ext_settlement_credit -> issue_settlement_credit_d3237287 ->
  computations[2] step 11 -> a passes_credit_issue entry of 302.89 and credit standing 435.32. charter_scope,
  required_documents and the computations name the same three policies in the same order.


MANUAL VALUE GATES (run after the per-task scripts went green; results recorded here).
  Length and breadth: surface goal (what the collective will put back on the pass) -> the settlement rule's own sentence
    makes the credit wait on the charge retained standing on the pass account -> the ledger shows no such charge ->
    the surrender rule's own sentence makes the charge wait on an application of credit against what the account has
    to collect -> the ledger shows none -> the credit application. Breadth: the tier's parameters, the credit entries
    and their reasons, the scans, two date spans (the cancellation window and the season) and three separate reads of
    the household's protection record in another difficulty.
  Customer's own write: the surrender is owner=user, which the blueprint fixes as the household's own act, and it
    completes on the call.
  Need and simulator boundary: the persona fixes the object (his only pass), the timing (settled on this call), the
    authorisation (he accepts resort credit and hands nothing else over) and that a write is wanted. He never states
    a figure, never orders the work and answers only what he is asked.
  Chronology: the job loss of 2 January, the claim paid out and the handful of days on the hill all point at seeded rows
    (insure claim payment of 2027-01-05, six scan entries). He knows nothing gold produces.
  Base eligibility and the time anchors: the credit validity and the cancellation window are copied verbatim from
    base with both boundary cases recorded; the window has two days left of thirty on the handling date.
  Authoritative facts and the business object: the record's own credit figure is deliberately stale and is not
    authority — the entries are; the protection plan is correlated to the pass it is written over.
  Reachability and no real-world waits: three writes under one frozen_time, nothing waiting on clearing or review.
  Factors, labels and baselines: the two method factors change how the pot is gathered and how the share of the
    season still to come and the gross amount are worked out; the four parameter factors select published figures;
    every tier rests on seeded rows; the stale credit figure, the six scan entries on five dates and the two window
    boundaries are the near-misses, each excluded by the wording of the rules alone; the withdrawn refund review of
    2027-01-04 seeded in revision 3 is the near-miss of the charge retained, offering a second date the cancellation
    window could be counted from.


REVISION 2 (source-layer audit of 2026-09-17, report at env/env_0004_ski_resort_operator/audits/policy_task/
season_pass_billing_desk/). Items closed that bear on this task:
  F1-1 (SOURCE-CHAIN RED) — the persona named the surrender, which is the hop-1 prerequisite problem, in its
    opening statement of need. The opening now asks only for what the collective will put back on the pass: "what
    you want is whatever the collective will put back to you on that pass, settled on this call rather than left
    hanging", and adds "How the collective gets there is their business, not yours". The surrender reaches the
    caller only through the agent, in a passive branch: "If the agent explains that the pass itself has to be given
    up before the collective will put anything back, you do not hesitate: you say yes, give the pass up". Both
    prerequisite problems are therefore derived from the policy surface — the settlement rule's sentence makes the
    credit wait on the charge retained, and the surrender rule's sentence makes that charge wait on an application
    of credit — and neither is announced by the customer. solvability_contract.gold_actions[step 9] now cites that
    passive line as the intent source, which is what an on_request policy requires, and prerequisite_closure's
    no_user_hint records the same.
  F1-2 / FIND-2 (SOURCE-POLICY and SOURCE-TASK RED) — the rules spoke of days taken while the bindings counted scan
    rows, and the charter's inherited sentences count a day once per date. The criterion is switched rather than the
    convention overridden: both rules now count lift scan entries, which is exactly what COUNT('passes_ledger',
    event_type='passes_scan') returns, and no rule multiplies the tier's day use deduction by a count of days. The
    deduction is taken once where it is taken at all, in the scan component of the charge retained and in the day
    use tier of the gross amount. Nothing in either policy now depends on the distinct-date convention, so base's
    "the day is counted on the first scan of that date" and passes_msr_season_scan_days stand untouched and
    unclaimed, and the second scan of 2026-12-27 has one reading only. The seed_consistency note on that row no
    longer asserts the day-counting rule. Bindings and factor ids were renamed with the wording: days_taken ->
    scans_taken, days_component_usd -> scan_component_usd, days_taken_a -> scans_counted, heavy_use_days ->
    heavy_use_scans, heavy_days -> heavy_scans, days_taken_component -> scan_component, days_taken_share ->
    scan_share. Every scored figure is unchanged: 127.57, 321.70, 302.89.
  F1-3 / FIND-4 (SOURCE-FACTOR RED) — gross_back_basis was divided by "the pass record carries no media serial",
    which no pass reaching this write can satisfy, and its second tier duplicated the fall-through's value. The
    ladder is redrawn on the tier's own refund basis, which the base charter publishes per tier: the pro rata basis
    with at least one lift scan entry gives the price committed to at the share of the season still to come; the day
    use basis gives the price committed to less the tier's day use deduction taken once; otherwise the price
    committed to in full. All three tiers are reachable across the tiers the collective sells, no two select the
    same outcome, and the factor's baseline is the fall-through. Revision 3 moved that fall-through again, to the
    standard method the collective would publish — the price committed to at the share of the season still to come,
    less the tier's day use deduction taken once — which gives 1197.86 on this world and a scored 143.19 in place of
    the 0.00 the round-1 day-use fall-through produced.
  F1-4 / FIND-1 (SOURCE-POLICY RED) — credit_pot_basis's rule tiers spoke of the number of distinct credit reasons
    while the binding tested for two particular reasons. The rule now states what the binding tests: a pot of every
    entry issued where credit has been issued to put a billing error right, the service-failure entries where it has
    not but service-failure credit stands, and the record's own figure otherwise. The ladder wording follows. The
    pot on this world is unchanged at 305.00.
  F1-5 / FIND-3 (SOURCE-POLICY RED) — "A single application is never less than the smallest single application the
    tier allows" stated an outcome no binding produced and left two readings. It is replaced by a sentence that
    names one outcome and is implemented: "Where the figure those deductions leave falls below the smallest single
    application the tier allows, no application is made at all and the whole of the pot stays on the pass record."
    compute now carries net_application_usd and a result branch on P('credit_minimum_redemption_usd'), with a
    compute_basis entry quoting the sentence. On this world 127.57 is above the tier's 50.00, so no figure moves.
  F1-6 / OBS-10 — the stale pass_credit_usd is kept deliberately and is declared in seed_consistency; the caller's
    own line, that he would rather the desk read it off their records than guess, is the re-check reaction that
    goes with it.
  F1-7 / OBS-1 — issue_settlement_credit_d3237287's docstring no longer states its position after the surrender; it
    now reads "Issue resort credit against a season pass record for what the collective returns to the household on
    that pass."
  F1-8 / OBS-4 — left as recorded: the pot bindings sum credit entries without a validity filter, which the
    restricted grammar cannot express in calendar days; base's own credit_within_validity gate still governs the
    write and both seeded entries are inside the tier's 365 days.
  F1-9 / OBS-9 — remaining_share_basis's second tier no longer turns on there being no day taken, which was the
    condition under which the binding it decides is never read. It now turns on a pass activated on or before the
    season opened whose tier admits the holder on fewer days than the season runs, and the share is then measured
    against the tier's operating days included. The tier can fire on a world where the share is genuinely consumed.
  F1-10 / OBS-6 — the ladder value entries that named a bare share now name the amount.
  Regression check after the changes: the three scored figures are unchanged (127.57 / 321.70 / 302.89); the edge
  load-bearing run still gives 352.75 without the credit application and 640.68 without the surrender; all sixteen
  factors still move their result; the terminal state is unchanged.

REVISION 3 (re-audit of 2026-09-17, revision_2 sections of the same report). Items closed that bear on this task:
  F1-11 (SOURCE-TASK RED) — evaluation_criteria's tracing for settlement_credit_usd still reasoned from "six days
    taken" (false on this world: six entries on five dates) and from "the record carries a media serial" (a
    condition the charter no longer tests). It is rewritten to the charter as it stands: the tier admits the holder
    on a hundred and fifty days against a season of a hundred and forty-nine, so the day-block tier does not apply;
    the pass became scannable after the season opened, so the share is 102 days against 129; the tier settles on the
    pro rata basis and the account shows six lift scan entries, so the gross amount is 1728.68 at that share with no
    day use deduction taken, 1366.86; six entries is at least the six the charter treats as heavy use, so nine
    tenths, 1230.17; less the charge retained 321.70 and the protection payout 620.00, then a twentieth of uplift:
    302.89. Nothing in the field now asserts a count of days or a media serial, and it no longer contradicts the
    seed note on the second scan of 2026-12-27, which says the same thing: entries, not dates, are what the rules
    count. The retained-charge tracing was rewritten in the same pass and now names the anchor the window runs from.
  F1-12 (observation) — evaluation_criteria[3].necessity no longer says "the scans are the days taken"; it says the
    lift scan entries are what the scan component and the scan share are counted from.
  F1-13 / OBS-9 (observation the reworker had wrongly reported closed) — the auditor is right: the replacement tier
    was dead across every variant, because remaining_share was read only on a branch requiring the pro rata basis
    while the only variants with fewer operating days than season days settle on the day use basis. Two changes
    close it. First, the gross amount's fall-through — the day use case — now multiplies by the share of the season
    still to come as well, so the four day-use tiers read remaining_share. Second, the share's own first tier is now
    the day-block rule the product actually implies: where the tier admits the holder on fewer days than the season
    runs, the share is the days the tier admits that the account shows unused, set against the days the tier admits,
    never below zero. On a Four-Day Flex pass with one day used that is three quarters, not the 25.5 the old
    formulation would have produced. The tier is reachable (Four-Day Flex 4 days, Midweek 107, both against a
    149-day season) and it reaches the scored figure through the fall-through branch of the gross amount.
  F1-14 (observation) — computations[0].factor_sensitivity[0].tier_taken said "credit issued under more than one
    reason", the very condition FIND-1 showed the binding did not test. It now carries the reworked ladder's own
    wording, "the pass account shows credit issued to put a billing error right".
  F1-15 (observation) — the second computation's near-miss, lost when the double scan became a counted entry, is
    restored by a record rather than by a boundary: initial_state.passes_requests carries a refund review the
    household raised on 2027-01-04 and withdrew. A reader who counts the cancellation window from the day the
    household first asked reaches the second day of a thirty-day window, takes the window share at as it stands
    rather than at once and a half, and books 245.80 instead of 321.70. The rule excludes it by naming the anchor —
    "counted from the day the application was recorded", 2026-12-09 — which is base's own anchor for that gate. The
    row is inert: it is withdrawn, no policy reads passes_requests and no tool writes it. A read node was added for
    it (find_pass_service_requests), which moved the three write steps from 7/9/11 to 8/10/12; every step index,
    prior_step reference and temporal entry moved with them.
  N-1 (observation) — passes_ext_settlement_credit.baseline.params still names day_use_deduction_usd, and after the
    revision-3 change to the gross amount's fall-through that key is once again a default of the standard method
    ("less the tier's day use deduction taken once"), so the key and the baseline paragraph agree.
  N-2 (observation) — the whole-computation baseline is no longer a full refund. The standard method now reads the
    price committed to at the share of the season still to come, less the tier's day use deduction taken once, which
    is what base's own refund basis describes; it gives 1014.39 on this world, definite and still far from gold.
  N-3 (observation) — passes_ext_credit_offset can no longer compute nothing where the deductions bite. The rule
    now says the application is raised to the tier's smallest single application, and where the pot or the amount
    still to collect is smaller than that, the smaller of the two is applied; compute implements it. Revision 4
    added the two floors that sentence needed: the pot is never below zero however many applications stand drawn
    against it, and the figure the fallback produces is never below zero either. The tool's
    Args wording moved from "a positive figure" to "never negative", so no reachable figure is outside the
    contract and no world leaves the downstream gate unsatisfiable. On this world 127.57 clears the 50.00 minimum,
    so nothing moves.
  N-4 (observation, recorded with reasons) — the ladders divide on lift scan entries while the amount they select
    is the tier's day use deduction. The deduction is taken once, never per entry, so no quantity is denominated in
    days and the charter is internally consistent; the alternative — inventing a per-scan retention of the
    collective's own — would be a rate with no base asset behind it, which the skill forbids outright.
  N-5 (observation, recorded with reasons) — the refusal count is taken over the three whole months ending on the
    handling date while max_declines_before_suspension is defined over a ninety-day window. The restricted grammar

user_scenario:
You are Alan Whitcombe, fifty-five, a project surveyor in Fort Collins, and until three weeks ago you had a job you had held for eleven years. The firm folded on the second of January and you were let go with everyone else. You are ringing the Granite Ridge guest services centre from the kitchen table, tired and businesslike rather than upset, and you get to the point quickly: you bought the big Collective Unlimited pass for yourself in December, the wage that was paying for it has gone, and what you want is whatever the collective will put back to you on that pass, settled on this call rather than left hanging. You are not asking for cash back and you do not argue about how it comes back; whatever the collective returns you will take, and if the agent explains it comes back as resort credit against the pass you say that is fine, you will use it on the children's lessons next winter. How the collective gets there is their business, not yours: you have never read the terms and you would not know where to start.

When the agent asks how to find the household you give the mobile number the collective has, 3035550168. If they ask you to prove who you are you read out your date of birth, 1971-07-03, and the passholder number off the front of your pass, GR41007391; the postal code 80525 is there too if they want a third. Asked which pass, you say it is the only one, in your own name, Alan Whitcombe. Asked when you last skied on it you say the third of January, the Saturday, and that you were on the hill a handful of days over the holidays; you cannot remember exactly how many and you say so rather than guess.

If the agent asks why the pass cannot go on, you say plainly that you lost your job at the start of the month, which is the whole reason. If they ask whether you took any protection out on the pass, you say yes, you added the pass protection when you bought it, that you put a claim in the day after the firm folded and that it has been paid out already; you do not know what the plan is called or what it paid, and you say so if pressed. You would rather they read all that off their own records than have you guess at it.

Whenever the agent tells you something has to be put right on the pass account before anything can come back to you, you say go ahead, that is what they are there for, and you do not ask what it comes to. If the agent explains that the pass itself has to be given up before the collective will put anything back, you do not hesitate: you say yes, give the pass up, that is what you are asking for, and the reason is the job going. If the agent tells you there is a charge the collective keeps, you accept it without quarrelling; you may say that you had hoped for more back, but you do not dispute a figure and you never suggest one of your own. When the agent hands a step over to you and asks you to do it yourself, you do it with the details they give you, confirming the reason is the job going. Once the agent tells you the credit is on the pass record, you say that is that, thank them for being straight with you, and end the call.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Select the household account from the mobile number the caller states and read back its reference, the account holder's profile and whether a payment method is stored.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Every pass record, pass account entry and protection plan on the call is reached from the household reference.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Record that the caller is the household on screen by checking the two details he states against the profile on file.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Nothing may be transacted on a household account until an in-session verification has passed.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the pass record: the tier, the state it stands in, the dates it was applied for and became scannable, the price committed to, the amount still to be collected, the resort credit the record shows standing and the media serial.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The application date the cancellation window runs from, the activation date the share of the season still to come is measured from, the price committed to, the amount still to be collected and the record's own credit figure are all read here.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the whole pass account: the amount placed on it when the plan was opened, every scan the pass admitted the holder on, and the credit entries issued against the record with the reason each was issued for.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The credit entries and their reasons are what the pot drawn on and the error credit held back rest on, the lift scan entries are what the scan component of the charge retained and the scan share of the gross amount are counted from, and the plan entry is what the amount still to collect is measured against; the record's own credit figure cannot be trusted against them.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the protection plan written over the pass: the plan held, the state it stands in, the value covered and the premium still to be collected.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The plan's state and the premium still to be collected decide the amount held back from the credit applied, and the plan's state decides the share at which its payout is taken off what comes back.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the entries on the protection account: the premium raised, the payment made against it, the cover loaded and the payout made on the settled claim.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The payout on the protection account is the figure taken off what comes back, and the premium entries confirm how much premium is still to be collected.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the service requests standing against the household's pass: what was asked for, the reason given, where each request stands and the moment it was registered.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: It settles that nothing is pending against the pass before it is given up, and it shows the request the household raised and withdrew on 2027-01-04 — the date a reader could mistake for the day the cancellation window runs from, which the terms anchor on the day the application was recorded instead.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the desk action that spends resort credit against a pass account so it can be called.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The first half of the unlock/call pair; it has no effect on the records.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Spend the resort credit standing on the pass record against the money the pass account still has to collect, dropping both the credit left and the amount still to be collected.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The figure applied is what the credit offset policy uniquely produces; the application it books is what the charge retained on the surrender is later measured against.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.pass_id: The household's only pass record. Basis: the tool's schema says of this argument 'the reference number of the season pass record the credit sits on and whose pass account is being reduced, as returned by the season pass lookup', and the pass lookup returns exactly one record on this household, in the caller's own name. Uniqueness: there is no second pass record to confuse it with.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.related_event_id: The reference of the credit entry of 2026-12-28 for 260.00 issued to put a service failure right. Basis: the tool's schema says of this argument 'the reference number of the pass account entry that issued the credit being spent, read from the pass account entry lookup', and the published terms say that where several credit entries sit on one pass, the entry closest to running out is applied first. Uniqueness: the account carries exactly two credit entries, issued on 2026-12-28 and 2027-01-02, both under the tier's validity of 365 days; the earlier of the two runs out first, so the application is drawn against the 2026-12-28 entry and no other reachable reference answers.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.credit_pot: service_recovery. Basis: the tool's schema lists the closed set and says of this value 'credit issued to put right a day or a service the collective failed to deliver', and the pass account entry the application is drawn against carries exactly that reason. Uniqueness: of the six labels, none is for an entry that touches no credit, pass_cancellation names credit issued because a pass was given up and none has been issued yet, downgrade_differential names a move to a lower tier the record does not show, protection_settlement names a claim settled in credit while the protection payout on this household went to the original payment method, and duplicate_charge names the other entry, of 2027-01-02, which the terms hold back rather than draw on.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.credit_applied_usd: 127.57. The pass account shows credit issued under two reasons, 260.00 to put a service failure right on 2026-12-28 and 45.00 to put a billing error right on 2027-01-02, so the pot is the sum of every credit entry issued less every application already drawn, 305.00 — not the 260.00 the pass record itself shows standing. The account shows no scheduled instalment presented and none refused, the first falling due on the tier's tenth of the month after the thirty-day first charge lag, so three quarters of the pot is drawn: 228.75. The 45.00 issued to put the billing error right is held back in full because the pass record still admits the holder, and the protection plan written over the pass stands with a settled claim and shows 56.18 of premium still to be collected, so that too is held back. 228.75 less 45.00 less 56.18 is 127.57, which is below the 1458.68 the account still has to collect and above the tier's smallest single application of 50.00.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.cancellation_reason: employment_loss. Basis: the tool's schema gives the closed set and says of this value 'the household has lost the employment the pass was bought on', and the caller says he lost his job at the start of the month, which is the whole reason. Uniqueness: guest_request would be the label where the household simply no longer wants the pass, which is not what he says; medical would need the holder to have been told they may not ski; relocation would need a permanent move away from the region; resort_closure would need the collective to have stopped running the season; and none would record no reason at all, which the caller has given.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.retained_charge_usd: 321.70. The charge base is the tier's cancellation fee of 150.00 reduced in the proportion the price committed to, 1728.68, bears to the tier's standard season price of 1879.00, giving 138.00, because the record was opened as a renewal and the price stands below the standard. The pass was applied for on 2026-12-09 and the handling date is the twenty-eighth day of the tier's thirty-day cancellation window, past two thirds of it, so the base is taken at once and a half: 207.00 — the window runs from the day the application was recorded, not from the day the household raised the refund review it withdrew on 2027-01-04. After the credit application the pass account still shows 1331.11 to collect against the 1458.68 placed on it when the plan was opened, which is at least eighty but below ninety-five in the hundred, so that figure is taken at once and a tenth: 227.70. The account shows six lift scan entries, at least the six the charter treats as heavy use, so the tier's day use deduction of 169.00 is retained in addition. A hundred and two of the season's hundred and forty-nine days still remain, at least two thirds, so the early-season allowance of 25.00 is settled against the charge, and the protection plan stands with a settled claim and a season benefit of eighty in the hundred of the value covered, so the charge is relieved by the 50.00 excess that plan carries. 227.70 plus 169.00 less 25.00 less 50.00 is 321.70.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.pass_id: The pass record just given up. Basis: the tool's schema says of this argument 'the reference number of the season pass record the credit is issued against, as returned by the season pass lookup'. Uniqueness: it is the household's only pass record and the one now standing given up.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.protection_plan_id: The protection plan record written over that pass. Basis: the tool's schema says of this argument 'the reference number of the protection plan record the collective checks the settlement against, as returned by the protection plan lookup', and the published terms answer a settlement to the collective's own protection records. Uniqueness: the protection lookup returns exactly one plan on this household, written over this pass.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.settlement_credit_usd: 302.90. The Collective Unlimited tier admits the holder on a hundred and fifty days, which is not fewer than a quarter of the season's hundred and forty-nine, so the pass is not the block of days whose share is taken as the whole; the pass became scannable on 2026-12-10, after the season opened on 2026-11-20, so the share still to come is the 102 days from the handling date to 2027-04-18 set against the 129 days from activation to that date. That tier settles what comes back on the pro rata basis and the pass account shows six lift scan entries, so the gross amount is the price committed to, 1728.68, multiplied by that share, with no day use deduction taken: 1366.86 to the cent. Six lift scan entries is at least the six the charter treats as heavy use, so nine tenths of it is taken. The charge retained on the surrender, 321.70, stands on the pass account and the account still shows an amount to collect, so the whole of it is taken off; the protection plan written over this pass stands with a settled claim, so the whole 620.00 its protection account shows paid out this season is taken off as well, leaving 288.48 to the cent. The three premium entries on that protection account are not payouts and do not enter. The pass account shows an amount placed on it to be collected by instalments and the price is still being collected, so that figure is increased by a twentieth. Every step is carried through unrounded and the figure is rounded to the cent once at the end, which gives 302.90; rounding the intermediate products instead would give a cent less, and the published terms round only once.

edges.condition: The pass account carries a charge entry raised for the pass being given up.
edges.policy_source: The resort credit issued when a pass is given up is worked out only after the pass account carries the charge retained on the pass being given up.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: At 2027-01-06 the pass account carries no charge raised for the pass being given up: its entries are the amount placed on it when the plan was opened, six lift scans and two credit entries, and the pass record still admits the holder with no reason recorded against it. While no such charge stands, the share at which it would be taken off sits on its fall-through of none and the amount coming back is overstated.

At that figure the outstanding share sits at its highest tier rather than the tier the world really warrants.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The credit application write books a passes_credit_redeem entry of 127.57 and lowers installment_balance_usd to 1331.11, which is below ninety-five in the hundred of the plan amount, so the outstanding share moves from once and a quarter to once and a tenth and the charge retained falls from 352.75 to 321.70.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a chain: the settlement credit depends on the surrender alone and the surrender on the credit application alone, so only one order is topological and there is nothing to reorder. Taking them in any other order changes the terminal state: surrendering before the credit is applied leaves the outstanding share at once and a quarter and the charge retained at 352.75, and issuing the settlement credit before the surrender finds no charge standing and gives 640.69. The reverse order is independently impossible, since the base rule on resort credit applies it only while the pass record has not reached the cancelled state.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the surrender write and replaying everything else leaves no charge retained on the pass account, so the offset share is none instead of the whole and the settlement credit rises from 302.90 to 640.69; the pass record also never reaches the given-up state, so the terminal status and closed date differ.

Skipping the credit application and replaying everything else leaves the amount still to collect at 1458.68, the whole of the plan amount, so the outstanding share is once and a quarter instead of once and a tenth and the charge retained rises from 321.70 to 352.75; the terminal ledger also lacks the application entry and the record keeps its credit.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: The caller raises one thing only: what the collective will put back to him on a pass he can no longer pay for. Nothing he volunteers names the surrender, the charge retained, the resort credit standing on the record, a service-recovery entry, an amount charged twice or a premium still to be collected, and he never asks whether something has to be done first — the opening request is 'what you want is whatever the collective will put back to you on that pass, settled on this call rather than left hanging'. That the pass itself must be given up before anything comes back is read out of the settlement rule's own sentence and reaches him only when the agent explains it, whereupon he answers in the pre-written passive branch 'If the agent explains that the pass itself has to be given up before the collective will put anything back, you do not hesitate: you say yes, give the pass up'. The same holds of the credit application: his only line on that ground is 'Whenever the agent tells you something has to be put right on the pass account before anything can come back to you, you say go ahead'.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: No task tool checks a prerequisite. apply_pass_credit_52fe36c9 reads the pass row only for the household reference, books the application and lowers the two balances whatever the record shows; give_up_season_pass_8c1a0eca books the charge and sets the record to the given-up state whether or not any credit has been applied, and tests nothing about the window, the protection record or the reason; issue_settlement_credit_d3237287 books the credit whatever state the record stands in and whatever the account carries. None of the three raises, refuses or hints, so an agent that issues the settlement credit first still gets a receipt and simply lands a different terminal hash.
